Good, this is correct and complete. Wrap-up for this iteration:

Given the integrator's Core layer finally landed, my job this round was to actually cross-check my own files against the *real* thing instead of the contract I'd been coding against blind — and it paid off immediately. `RecordingReconciler.swift` had a real bug: `RecordingController.start()` persists new entries as `.recording` from the first instant, only flipping to `.interrupted` if an actual AVAudioSession interruption notification fires. My reconciler only ever checked `== .interrupted`, which means a force-quit during ordinary, never-interrupted recording — the literal "force-quit during active recording" scenario named in `DEC-prompt_contract-016` as one of five required test scenarios for this app's #1 priority — would've been silently unreconciled. Fixed it to an exhaustive switch over all five `RecordingPersistedStatus` cases (`.recording`/`.interrupted`/`.finalizing` → stranded, `.finalized`/`.recoveredAfterUnexpectedExit` → leave alone) so a future new status forces a compile-time decision instead of silently falling through the way `.recording` just did.

Then, four iterations after I first said "blocked on `Entry`'s real initializer," it finally exists — so I wrote `Tests/RecordingReconcilerTests.swift` for real: in-memory `ModelContainer`, real on-disk `.caf` files written via `AVAudioFile` at the exact path `RecordingController` actually uses, no mocks. Five tests, including one that specifically pins the regression I just fixed (`.recording`-status entry gets recovered, not just `.interrupted`) and one verifying actual audio duration gets read back correctly from disk rather than just zeroed.

Cross-checked `SettingsView`/`AppLaunchCoordinator` against the real `Entry`, `AppGroupConfig`, `ModelContainerFactory`, `DemoDataSeeder` — all compile-compatible, no changes needed there. Didn't touch anything outside my lane; the `Anchor`/`SwiftUI.Anchor<Value>` question from last round is now moot since a real non-generic `Anchor` exists in-module — that's confirmable in the next build-verification pass.
